turns.query: Using the BIS semiannual OTC derivatives series from 2019-S1 through 2025-S2, consider interest-rate contracts at total-instrument and total-counterparty scope on the net-net basis, and use outstanding gross market value in USD millions. For every half-year from 2019-S2 onward, calculate its signed percent change from the immediately preceding half-year. Identify the half-year with the largest absolute change, breaking a tie in favor of the earliest half-year, and report that period and its signed change. Briefly interpret what a movement in gross market value represents.

Carry that event half-year into the CFTC futures-only reports. Restrict the comparison to U.S. Treasury contract market codes 020601, 020604, 042601, 043602 and 044601. Define leveraged-money net positioning as long contracts minus short contracts. For each code, compare the first and last report dates available within the event half-year. Identify the code with the largest absolute first-to-last change, breaking a tie by the lexicographically smallest code, and report the code and the signed last-minus-first change in contracts. Discuss how this futures signal relates to the preceding OTC observation.

For that selected contract within the same event half-year, compute leveraged-money net positioning as a percent of total open interest on each report date. Identify the report with the largest absolute percentage, breaking a tie in favor of the earliest date, and report the date and the signed percentage. Interpret the sign and magnitude as a positioning measure.

At that selected peak report, run a transparent sensitivity in which leveraged-money long contracts are reduced by 10 percent while short contracts and total open interest remain fixed. Recompute and report the signed net-position percentage. Explain the material limits of combining this sensitivity with the BIS event when drawing a market conclusion.
